posts.topic: The best teardown of the month
posts.why: Re-cutting the month's best asset rewards the audience that watched it.

tiktok.hook: The best teardown of the month, re-cut sharper. Same business, three fixes, twenty seconds.
tiktok.vo: The best teardown of the month, re-cut in twenty seconds. The bakery with the four paragraphs and the one real headline: bread out of the oven at six, Agege. The problem was never the site, it was that the best sentence they own was in a caption and not on the page. Fix: the headline, the hours, and the price of a loaf. That is the whole month of teardowns in one example.
tiktok.cap: Their best sentence was in a caption, not on the page. That is most businesses.
tiktok.body: Four paragraphs about quality, and the real headline was bread at six in the morning in Agege. The best sentence they own was in a caption, not on the page.

instagram.cap:
The re-cut is sharper than the original and the diagnosis is identical: the specific sentence is buried and the generic one is at the top.

Re-cutting the month's best teardown, because it is still the most common problem.

facebook.body:
The best teardown of the month, re-cut.

A bakery with four paragraphs about quality and tradition. The actual reason anyone goes: bread out of the oven at six in the morning, in Agege.

The best sentence they own was in a caption, not on the page.

That is most businesses. Including, probably, yours.

What is your buried sentence?

posts.why: Naming the cost is the most credible transparency available.

tiktok.hook: Three hundred and thirty posts this month. Here is what it cost in hours and naira.
tiktok.vo: Three hundred and thirty ideas, nine hundred and ninety published pieces, and here is what it cost. Roughly six hours a day of writing and filming, about two hundred thousand naira in time if I charged myself my own rate, and three weekends I did not have. Worth it is not a question I can answer in one video, and anybody who answers it in one video is selling something.
tiktok.cap: ~6 hours a day, ~₦200,000 of my own time, 3 weekends. Worth it is a longer conversation.
tiktok.body: Six hours a day of writing and filming, about two hundred thousand naira in time at my own rate, three weekends gone. Whether it was worth it is not a question one video can answer.

instagram.cap:
The cost is the part that is always missing from these retrospectives, and it is the part that decides whether you should try it.

Anybody who tells you the ROI in one post is selling you something.

facebook.body:
330 ideas this month. 990 published pieces. Here is what it cost.

Roughly six hours a day of writing and filming. About ₦200,000 in time, if I charged myself my own rate. Three weekends I did not have.

Whether it was worth it is not a question I can answer in one post — and anybody who answers it in one post is selling something.

What is your honest cost?

posts.topic: The five posts that produced every conversation
posts.why: Naming all five is the most useful thing an account can publish.

tiktok.hook: Five posts produced every conversation this month. Here they all are.
tiktok.vo: Five posts produced every conversation this month. The five lines every quote needs. The day three message, word for word. The four answer profile setup. The two fixes worth an hour in any business. And the one hour test before buying anything. Notice that all five are lists or scripts, and none of them are opinions, which is the entire content strategy and it took me four weeks to believe it.
tiktok.cap: Five posts. All lists or scripts. Zero opinions. That is the finding.
tiktok.body: Quote lines, the day-three message, the four-answer profile, the two fixes, the one-hour test. All lists or scripts, zero opinions, and it took four weeks to believe it.

instagram.cap:
Four of the five are reusable by anyone in any business, which is exactly why they travelled further than anything else.

Save this one. It is the whole month compressed.

facebook.body:
Five posts produced every conversation this month:

1. The five lines every quote needs
2. The day-three message, word for word
3. The four-answer profile setup
4. The two fixes worth an hour in any business
5. The one-hour test before buying anything

Notice: all lists or scripts. None of them opinions.

That is the entire content strategy, and it took four weeks to believe it.

posts.why: Normalises the flat line, which is the most useful thing to normalise.

tiktok.hook: Most of our posts did nothing. That is not a failure, it is the job.
beats: You cannot pick it in advance
tiktok.vo: Most of our posts did nothing, and that is not a failure, it is the job. Twenty percent of anything carries eighty percent of the result, and you cannot pick the twenty percent in advance, which is the only honest argument for volume. What you can do is keep a sheet, notice which twenty percent showed up, and then do that again on purpose.
tiktok.cap: You cannot pick the 20% in advance. You can notice it afterwards and repeat it.
tiktok.body: Twenty percent carries eighty, and you cannot pick the twenty in advance. Volume is the only honest way to find it, and the sheet is the only way to keep it.

slides: You find it after, not before
instagram.cap:
This is why a flat week is not evidence that the strategy failed. It is evidence that you have not yet found the twenty percent.

Volume is a search strategy, not an ambition.

facebook.body:
Most of our posts did nothing this month. That is not a failure, it is the job.

Twenty percent of anything carries eighty percent of the result, and you cannot pick the twenty percent in advance — which is the only honest argument for volume.

What you can do is keep a sheet, notice which twenty percent showed up, and do that again on purpose.

Do you keep the sheet?

posts.topic: The message that made the month
posts.why: One real message, anonymised, is worth more than any summary.

tiktok.hook: The message that made the month, anonymised and quoted exactly.
tiktok.vo: The message that made the month came from a tailor who watched three videos, changed her reply time from about a day to under an hour, and had two customers who had gone quiet come back and order. She sent me a screenshot of the chat. That is the entire result of the month, from my side, and it is small and it is real, which is the only kind of result I am willing to put on camera.
tiktok.cap: Reply time from a day to an hour. Two quiet customers came back.
tiktok.body: A tailor changed her reply time from about a day to under an hour. Two customers who had gone quiet came back and ordered. Small, real, and checkable.

instagram.cap:
This is the whole theory of the month in one example: a change that costs nothing and can be verified by the person who made it.

One behaviour change in one business beats a thousand views.

facebook.body:
The message that made the month came from a tailor.

She watched three videos, changed her reply time from about a day to under an hour, and two customers who had gone quiet came back and ordered.

She sent a screenshot of the chat.

That is the entire result of the month from my side. Small, real, checkable.

posts.why: One thing, not a list, is the harder and better answer.

tiktok.hook: One thing we would do differently from day one: film a week in advance.
beats: Because filming daily broke the writing
tiktok.vo: If we started again, one thing would change: we would film a week in advance. Not more ideas, not better hooks, just a week of buffer. Filming daily meant the writing got squeezed into whatever time was left, which is backwards, because the writing is the part that decides whether anything works. The buffer is the whole improvement.
tiktok.cap: One change: film a week ahead. The writing was what suffered.
tiktok.body: Filming daily squeezed the writing into whatever time was left, which is backwards. The buffer is the whole improvement, and it costs one weekend.

instagram.cap:
Batching is unglamorous and it is the difference between a month that survives contact with a busy week and one that collapses in week two.

The thing that gets squeezed is always the thing that matters most.

facebook.body:
One thing we would do differently from day one: film a week in advance.

Not more ideas. Not better hooks. A week of buffer.

Filming daily meant the writing got squeezed into whatever time was left — which is backwards, because the writing decides whether anything works.

Have you ever tried batching?

posts.why: Retiring something on camera is a commitment device.

tiktok.hook: There was a format nobody watched. We are retiring it on camera so we cannot quietly bring it back.
tiktok.vo: There was one format nobody watched: the four minute explainer. It got views, nobody finished it, and not one conversation came out of it. So we are retiring it on camera, which is the only way to make a decision stick, because a decision nobody saw is a decision you can quietly reverse in week three when you are tired.
tiktok.cap: Retired on camera: the four-minute explainer. Nobody finished it.
tiktok.body: It got views, nobody finished it, and no conversation came from it. Retiring it on camera because a decision nobody saw is one you can quietly reverse in week three.

instagram.cap:
The public statement is not for the audience. It is for the version of you who will be tired in three weeks.

Publish your decisions or you will reverse them quietly.

facebook.body:
There was one format nobody watched: the four-minute explainer.

It got views. Nobody finished it. Not one conversation came out of it.

So we are retiring it on camera — which is the only way to make a decision stick, because a decision nobody saw is a decision you can quietly reverse when you are tired.

What should you retire?

posts.topic: Have you seen any of this
posts.why: Reading out the nos is what makes the yeses mean something.

tiktok.hook: I asked people if they had seen any of this account. Most had not.
beats: Two had seen the bakery one
tiktok.vo: I asked people on the street if they had seen any of this account. Most had not, which is honest and worth saying out loud in a month of posting nine hundred and ninety pieces. Two had seen the bakery teardown, and one man had gone home and fixed his Google listing because of a video. Out of everyone I asked, that is the number. It is small. It is real.
tiktok.cap: Most had not seen it. One had fixed his listing. That is the honest reach.
tiktok.body: Most had not seen any of it. Two had seen the bakery teardown. One had gone home and fixed his Google listing. That is the number, and it is small and real.

instagram.cap:
Reporting the nos makes the yeses credible, which is the entire reason to do this on camera rather than in text.

Reach is smaller than the dashboard makes it feel. Say so.

facebook.body:
I asked people on the street whether they had seen any of this account.

Most had not. Which is honest and worth saying out loud after a month of nearly a thousand pieces.

Two had seen the bakery teardown. One man had gone home and fixed his Google listing because of a video.

Out of everyone I asked, that is the number. Small. Real.

posts.why: The largest refusal deserves the largest slot.

tiktok.hook: The biggest thing we declined this month was a retainer, and saying no cost us more than anything else.
beats: For work we did not believe in
tiktok.vo: The biggest thing we declined this month was a monthly retainer, the kind that pays the rent. The work was advertising a product I did not think worked, to people who could not easily afford it. I said no on a Tuesday and regretted it by Thursday, and then a week later somebody from that same industry asked us to do the opposite, which is not a moral reward, it is just what happens when you are known for saying no.
tiktok.cap: A retainer, declined. Regretted it by Thursday. Still the right call.
tiktok.body: Advertising a product I did not think worked, to people who could not easily afford it. Declined on a Tuesday, regretted by Thursday, and still the right call.

slides: Work: product I did not believe
instagram.cap:
The discomfort of turning down money is immediate and the benefit is not, which is why so few people do it and why it is worth a post.

You can regret a decision and still be right about it.

facebook.body:
The biggest thing we declined this month was a monthly retainer — the kind that pays the rent.

The work was advertising a product I did not think worked, to people who could not easily afford it.

I said no on a Tuesday and regretted it by Thursday.

A week later, somebody in the same industry asked us to do the opposite.

That is not a moral reward. It is just what happens when you are known for saying no.

posts.topic: How to run this yourself in December
posts.why: Giving the system away is the strongest possible closing move.

tiktok.hook: How to run this yourself in December: four shows, one sheet, eleven slots.
tiktok.vo: How to run this yourself in December. Pick four formats you can repeat: a fix, a list, a story, and an honest ad. Put them in one spreadsheet with a date and a time for every slot. Post eleven times a day if you can, five if you cannot. Keep sixty percent entertaining, thirty teaching, ten selling. Then do it for thirty days and read the sheet on the thirty first. That is the whole system, and it is free.
tiktok.cap: Four formats · one sheet · 60/30/10 · thirty days. That is the whole system.
tiktok.body: A fix, a list, a story, an honest ad. One spreadsheet with dates and times. Sixty percent entertaining, thirty teaching, ten selling. Thirty days, then read the sheet.

instagram.cap:
None of it requires software, a team, or a budget. It requires a sheet, a decision about formats, and thirty days of not changing the plan.

Screenshot this. It is the entire month, in a form you can run.

facebook.body:
How to run this yourself in December:

Pick four formats you can repeat — a fix, a list, a story, an honest ad.
Put them in one spreadsheet with a date and time for every slot.
Post eleven times a day if you can. Five if you cannot.
Keep it 60% entertaining, 30% teaching, 10% selling.
Do it for thirty days, then read the sheet.

That is the whole system, and it is free.
